stages.title: 01 · Sentence foundations
stages.note: Start here, or tick the basics you already understand. The first link is the main lesson; older alternatives are optional.

lessons.topic: は + です: your first sentence
lessons.description: Build “X is Y” sentences and understand the role of a topic marker.

lessons.topic: Questions with か
lessons.description: Ask yes/no and “what is…” questions in polite and casual speech.

lessons.topic: これ・それ・あれ
lessons.description: Point to this, that, and things farther away; distinguish polite direction words.

lessons.topic: この・その・あの + noun
lessons.description: Choose between a standalone demonstrative and a word placed before a noun.

lessons.topic: Possession and noun links: の
lessons.description: Connect nouns to express possession and relationships.

lessons.topic: Noun negation: じゃない
lessons.description: Say that something is not a particular thing, in casual and polite forms.

lessons.topic: い-adjectives and な-adjectives
lessons.description: Describe things and attach the right kind of adjective to a noun.

lessons.topic: Negative adjectives
lessons.description: Say “not expensive” or “not quiet” using the two adjective patterns.

lessons.topic: Past and past-negative adjectives
lessons.description: Describe how things were and how they were not.

lessons.topic: Adjective conjugation checkpoint
lessons.description: Test adjective negatives and past forms before adding more grammar.

lessons.topic: ある・いる vs です; がない vs じゃない
lessons.description: Distinguish existence from identity and living things from other things.

lessons.topic: Past noun sentences: だった・でした
lessons.description: Review “was” and “was not” for nouns; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Pronouns and omitted subjects
lessons.description: Choose natural ways to refer to people and learn when pronouns are inappropriate.

stages.title: 02 · Verbs and basic particles
stages.note: Learn the plain and polite forms that later lessons build on.

lessons.topic: Verb basics and を
lessons.description: Recognize basic verbs and mark the thing affected by an action.

lessons.topic: Polite verbs: ます
lessons.description: Turn dictionary forms into polite verb forms.

lessons.topic: Polite negatives: ません
lessons.description: Say that you do not do something politely.

lessons.topic: Polite past: ました・ませんでした
lessons.description: Talk about actions you did or did not do.

lessons.topic: に・で・と: first uses
lessons.description: Mark destinations, places of action, tools, and companions.

lessons.topic: Plain negatives: ない
lessons.description: Form informal negatives for the different verb groups.

lessons.topic: Plain past negative: なかった
lessons.description: Say what did not happen in casual Japanese.

lessons.topic: Negative-verb checkpoint
lessons.description: Check your recall of the plain negative conjugations.

lessons.topic: Verb nominalization: の + adjective
lessons.description: Treat an action as a noun to say that doing it is fun or difficult.

lessons.topic: 上手・下手・得意・苦手
lessons.description: Describe skills and preferences without treating these expressions as interchangeable.

lessons.topic: こと vs の: full nominalizer contrast
lessons.description: Distinguish where these nominalizers can be used; related coverage exists, but no dedicated matching public video was verified.

lessons.topic: Adverbs: adjective く / に + verb
lessons.description: Describe how an action happens; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: に vs で: deeper comparison
lessons.description: Resolve location, destination, means, and other particle choices in context.

lessons.topic: は vs が: deeper comparison
lessons.description: Distinguish topics, subjects, contrast, and new information.

lessons.topic: Particle checkpoint, including へ・まで・から
lessons.description: Review the roles of common particles across complete sentences.

lessons.topic: Adjective nouns: さ
lessons.description: Turn a quality into a noun; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 03 · The て-form toolkit
stages.note: Make requests, link actions, and talk about ongoing actions and past experiences.

lessons.topic: Conjugate the て-form
lessons.description: Learn the endings for each verb group; use the older group-by-group lessons if needed.

lessons.topic: Requests with てください
lessons.description: Use the て-form for basic requests; this older lesson also introduces ongoing actions.

lessons.topic: Ongoing actions: ている・ています
lessons.description: Describe what someone is doing using the plain and polite forms.

lessons.topic: Present/future vs ている
lessons.description: Avoid using the simple non-past form when you mean an action in progress.

lessons.topic: Not yet: ていない
lessons.description: Say an action has not happened yet using the negative of ている.

lessons.topic: ます and て-form checkpoint
lessons.description: Test conjugations; the short video offers a quick extra drill.

lessons.topic: Plain past: た-form
lessons.description: Build informal past tense from familiar conjugation patterns.

lessons.topic: Experience: たことがある
lessons.description: Say that you have done something before.

lessons.topic: Representative actions: たり…たりする
lessons.description: List examples of things you do without giving an exhaustive list.

lessons.topic: Connect adjectives with くて・で
lessons.description: Join descriptions without using the noun connector と.

lessons.topic: Connect actions and ideas: て・と・や・し・も
lessons.description: Choose the right “and/also” construction for verbs, nouns, and reasons.

lessons.topic: Permission: てもいい
lessons.description: Ask if you may do something and give permission.

lessons.topic: Beginner verb overview: wants, invitations, “don’t”
lessons.description: Review common verb patterns together, including ways to tell someone not to do something.

lessons.topic: Prohibition: てはいけない・ちゃだめ
lessons.description: Say an action is not allowed; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: ないで vs なくて
lessons.description: Distinguish doing something without an action from a negative connection or reason; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 04 · Wants, plans, and everyday choices
stages.note: Use the forms you know to express what you want, can do, and intend to do.

lessons.topic: Want to: たい
lessons.description: Express your wish to do an action.

lessons.topic: Do not want to: たくない
lessons.description: Negate wishes and conjugate the たい expression.

lessons.topic: Can: potential forms and ことができる
lessons.description: Express ability and distinguish verb-group potential endings.

lessons.topic: Invitations and volitional forms
lessons.description: Make “let’s…” suggestions and “shall I…?” offers.

lessons.topic: Plans: つもり・予定・ようと思う
lessons.description: Talk about intentions and arrangements, and compare how definite they sound.

lessons.topic: Have to: obligation and necessity
lessons.description: Express duties and needs; the lesson also contrasts past obligations and regrets.

lessons.topic: No need: なくてもいい
lessons.description: Say that someone does not have to do something.

lessons.topic: Advice: たほうがいい・ないほうがいい
lessons.description: Recommend an action or advise against it.

lessons.topic: Comparisons: より・ほうが
lessons.description: Say that one thing is more or better than another.

lessons.topic: Only: だけ vs しか
lessons.description: Limit a statement while choosing the correct positive or negative form.

lessons.topic: Want a thing: ほしい; others’ wishes: たがる
lessons.description: Distinguish wanting an object from an action and describing someone else’s desire; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Go to do: verb stem + に行く
lessons.description: Express the purpose of a trip; Misa’s old #34 is documented, but its public video could not be verified.

lessons.topic: Too much / easy or hard to do: すぎる・やすい・にくい
lessons.description: Add these productive endings to describe excess or difficulty; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: 何か・誰か・何も・誰も
lessons.description: Express indefinite people or things and their negatives; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Approximate amounts: くらい・ぐらい・ごろ
lessons.description: Distinguish rough quantities from approximate times; no dedicated matching public comparison found.

stages.title: 05 · Longer sentences
stages.note: Combine clauses before moving on to more abstract meanings.

lessons.topic: Relative clauses and word order
lessons.description: Put a descriptive clause before a noun to build longer Japanese sentences.

lessons.topic: が / の inside relative clauses
lessons.description: Recognize this subject-marker alternation after studying relative clauses; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Reasons: から vs ので
lessons.description: Explain why something happens and compare natural ways to ask why.

lessons.topic: Contrast: でも・けど・が・のに
lessons.description: Connect contrasting ideas and distinguish neutral “but” from unexpected results.

lessons.topic: Before: 前に vs 前で
lessons.description: Distinguish time expressions from positions in front of something.

lessons.topic: Quotation: と言う・と思う・って
lessons.description: Report statements and thoughts; some linked lessons use these forms, but no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Embedded questions: か・かどうか
lessons.description: Put “what/where…” or “whether…” inside another sentence; an official text article exists, but no matching public video found.

lessons.topic: After: てから・たあとで
lessons.description: Place one event after another and clarify their sequence; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Even if: ても・でも
lessons.description: Keep the result true despite a condition; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 06 · If, when, and purpose
stages.note: Follow Misa’s four-part conditional sequence, then apply it to goals and wishes.

lessons.topic: Conditional 1: と vs とき
lessons.description: Express regular consequences and compare “if” with “when.”

lessons.topic: Conditional 2: たら
lessons.description: Use たら for conditions and events that happen after something else.

lessons.topic: Conditional 3: なら
lessons.description: Respond to an assumed situation or information someone gives you.

lessons.topic: Conditional 4: ば・もし
lessons.description: Form ば conditions, compare all four patterns, and introduce counterfactual wishes.

lessons.topic: Purpose 1: ために vs ように
lessons.description: Distinguish intentional goals from desired outcomes.

lessons.topic: Purpose 2: ように vs のに
lessons.description: Extend purpose expressions and compare their grammatical connections.

lessons.topic: Hopes: といい・ますように
lessons.description: Express hopes for yourself and other people.

lessons.topic: During / while there is time: 間・間に・うちに
lessons.description: Place actions within a time window; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 07 · Giving, receiving, and voice
stages.note: Learn perspective before combining passive and causative grammar.

lessons.topic: Giving and receiving: あげる・くれる・もらう
lessons.description: Choose the verb that matches the giver, receiver, and speaker’s viewpoint.

lessons.topic: Favors: てあげる・てくれる・てもらう
lessons.description: Describe doing an action for someone and receiving a favor.

lessons.topic: Want someone to: てほしい vs てもらいたい
lessons.description: Request or express a wish for someone else’s action.

lessons.topic: Transitive vs intransitive verbs
lessons.description: Distinguish someone changing a thing from a thing changing on its own.

lessons.topic: Passive: れる・られる
lessons.description: Describe what happens to someone and how an action affects them.

lessons.topic: Causative 1: せる・させる
lessons.description: Say that someone makes another person do something.

lessons.topic: Causative 2: permission and favors
lessons.description: Combine “let someone…” with giving and receiving expressions.

lessons.topic: Causative-passive
lessons.description: Say that someone was made or forced to do something.

stages.title: 08 · Time, state, and change
stages.note: Extend familiar verb forms to describe preparation, results, and intention.

lessons.topic: Try: てみる vs ようとする
lessons.description: Distinguish trying an action out from attempting to do it.

lessons.topic: Preparation: ておく・とく
lessons.description: Do something in advance and recognize the common spoken contraction.

lessons.topic: Resulting states: てある vs ている vs ておく
lessons.description: Connect transitivity with results, current states, and preparation.

lessons.topic: Completion or regret: てしまう・ちゃう
lessons.description: Describe finishing an action or doing something unintentionally.

lessons.topic: Just did: たばかり vs たところ
lessons.description: Distinguish subjective recency from the immediate stage after an action.

lessons.topic: Movement and change: ていく vs てくる
lessons.description: Express direction relative to the speaker and changes over time.

lessons.topic: Unchanged state: まま vs ながら vs て
lessons.description: Describe an action done with a state continuing; compare simultaneous actions.

lessons.topic: Decisions: ことにする vs ことになる
lessons.description: Distinguish a personal decision from something being decided or arranged.

lessons.topic: Past intention: たつもり vs つもりだった
lessons.description: Contrast believing you did something with having intended to do it.

lessons.topic: わかる vs 知っている
lessons.description: Distinguish understanding from having knowledge and use the appropriate aspect.

lessons.topic: Become / make: くなる・になる・くする・にする
lessons.description: Describe changes in qualities and deliberate changes; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: New ability and habits: ようになる・ようにする
lessons.description: Describe becoming able to do something and making an effort to do it; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: Action stages: ところだ・ているところだ
lessons.description: Say an action is about to begin or is in progress; the linked たところ lesson does not verify full coverage of this family.

lessons.topic: Action phases: 始める・出す・続ける・終わる
lessons.description: Describe starting, continuing, or finishing an action; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: 見える・聞こえる vs potential forms
lessons.description: Distinguish visibility and audibility from ability; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 09 · Explanation and uncertainty
stages.note: Add context, inference, appearance, and conversational expectations.

lessons.topic: Explanatory の・んだ・んです
lessons.description: Give background, seek explanations, and soften how you enter a conversation.

lessons.topic: じゃない・じゃん beyond negation
lessons.description: Recognize confirmation, surprise, and other conversational meanings.

lessons.topic: んじゃない vs じゃないの
lessons.description: Express a guess and distinguish question or confirmation nuances.

lessons.topic: でしょう・だろう
lessons.description: Express probability or seek agreement, and compare with ね.

lessons.topic: かもしれない vs 多分
lessons.description: Express uncertainty and choose between “maybe” and “probably.”

lessons.topic: Expected result: はず
lessons.description: Say what should be true based on the situation.

lessons.topic: Appearance: そう
lessons.description: Say that something looks a certain way, including negative appearance forms.

lessons.topic: Hearsay: そうだ vs らしい
lessons.description: Report information you heard and distinguish forms of indirect evidence.

lessons.topic: Resemblance: みたい・よう・らしい・っぽい
lessons.description: Compare similarity, typical qualities, and tendencies.

lessons.topic: かな・かしら
lessons.description: Express wondering rather than asking a direct question; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 10 · Intermediate nuance and selected N2 topics
stages.note: These are later studies, not a complete N3/N2/N1 exam syllabus.

lessons.topic: わけだ 1: “that explains it”
lessons.description: Make sense of new information by drawing a conclusion.

lessons.topic: わけだ 2: “which means…”
lessons.description: Restate a consequence and summarize a line of reasoning.

lessons.topic: わけではない・わけがない
lessons.description: Contrast “it does not mean…” with “there is no way…”.

lessons.topic: べき vs はず vs ほうがいい
lessons.description: Distinguish a duty or judgment from an expectation or recommendation.

lessons.topic: ばかり・てばかり
lessons.description: Describe doing only one thing and contrast other “only” expressions.

lessons.topic: ほど…ない
lessons.description: Make “not as…” comparisons and express strong evaluations.

lessons.topic: ほど vs ぐらい
lessons.description: Express degree and “so…that…” results.

lessons.topic: ずにはいられない vs つい…ちゃう
lessons.description: Say you cannot help doing something or do it involuntarily.

lessons.topic: どうしても
lessons.description: Express determination or an inability despite effort.

lessons.topic: なんて vs なんか
lessons.description: Express surprise, dismissal, or a negative evaluation in conversation.

lessons.topic: もの・もん・んだもん
lessons.description: Justify yourself or give an emotionally colored explanation.

lessons.topic: ものだ・たものだ
lessons.description: Talk about general expectations and reminisce about past habits.

lessons.topic: 多い vs 多く vs いっぱい vs たくさん
lessons.description: Use quantities naturally with nouns and verbs.

lessons.topic: More ways to say “a lot”
lessons.description: Compare common quantity expressions in context.

lessons.topic: すべて・全部・みんな・ずっと
lessons.description: Distinguish “all/everything” expressions from continuity over time.

lessons.topic: わけにはいかない
lessons.description: Express being unable to do something for social or situational reasons; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: たびに・につれて・とともに
lessons.description: Link repeated events or changes that progress together; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: おかげで・せいで
lessons.description: Attribute a positive or negative outcome to a cause; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: はずがない・に違いない・に決まっている
lessons.description: Extend expressions of strong inference and certainty; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

lessons.topic: ば…ほど
lessons.description: Link increasing degrees; related degree lessons are available, but no dedicated matching public comparison found.

stages.title: 11 · Register and natural conversation
stages.note: Apply the grammar in social situations; these lessons include usage as well as grammar.

lessons.topic: Sentence endings: よ・ね・よね・っけ
lessons.description: Choose an ending for information, agreement, or recalling something.

lessons.topic: When to use だ・だね・だな・だよ
lessons.description: Distinguish the plain copula from sentence-ending nuances.

lessons.topic: Sentence-final ぞ
lessons.description: Recognize assertive or dramatic speech and its social implications.

lessons.topic: Commands and なさい
lessons.description: Compare command forms with softer or conventional expressions.

lessons.topic: Requests beyond ください
lessons.description: Choose a request that fits the situation and relationship.

lessons.topic: Keigo: respectful and humble forms
lessons.description: Distinguish raising someone else’s status from lowering your own actions.

lessons.topic: Restaurant speech and keigo in practice
lessons.description: Follow an order and recognize the polite forms used by staff and customers.

lessons.topic: Short keigo review
lessons.description: Review a compact set of restaurant and café expressions.

lessons.topic: Polite vs casual vs rude speech
lessons.description: Compare how the same communicative goal changes with register.

lessons.topic: Tokyo casual speech
lessons.description: Recognize contractions and phrasing used in informal conversation.

lessons.topic: Everyday casual expressions
lessons.description: Extend your informal conversation toolkit with common spoken expressions.

lessons.topic: Kansai vs standard Japanese
lessons.description: Recognize regional forms after establishing standard Japanese grammar.

lessons.topic: Changing the subject
lessons.description: Choose formal or casual ways to introduce a new topic.

lessons.topic: Formal writing: である
lessons.description: Recognize the written copula after learning ordinary plain and polite speech; no dedicated matching public lesson found.

stages.title: 12 · Grammar in context and review
stages.note: Optional consolidation. Revisit these when you finish a stage rather than racing through every video.

lessons.topic: N5 grammar checkpoint
lessons.description: Use a mixed grammar, vocabulary, and kanji test to find weak basics.

lessons.topic: N4 grammar checkpoint
lessons.description: Check how intermediate-beginner grammar works in test questions.

lessons.topic: N4 verb-pattern review
lessons.description: Practice たら, たり, てみる, ておく, and other learned patterns.

lessons.topic: N5/N4 reading and listening review
lessons.description: Recognize familiar grammar while working through connected language.

lessons.topic: Informal conversation practice
lessons.description: Listen for grammar as it appears in casual exchanges.

lessons.topic: N4 conversation 1
lessons.description: Consolidate N4-level structures in a listening lesson.

lessons.topic: N4 conversation 2
lessons.description: Continue applying the same structures in another conversation.

lessons.topic: Formal and informal listening checkpoint
lessons.description: Test comprehension across contrasting speech styles.

lessons.topic: N4 story practice: Hanasaka Jiisan
lessons.description: Read and listen to a folktale adapted for N4 practice.

lessons.topic: N3 story practice: Hanasaka Jiisan
lessons.description: Revisit the story with more demanding language.

lessons.topic: N3 grammar and integrated practice
lessons.description: Apply grammar in a combined vocabulary, reading, and listening lesson.

lessons.topic: N3–N2 listening practice
lessons.description: Work through a longer listening lesson using more advanced language.

lessons.topic: Travel phrases with grammar
lessons.description: Apply practical sentence patterns to travel situations.

lessons.topic: Anime trailer analysis: DAN DA DAN
lessons.description: Notice grammar and natural phrasing in a short authentic clip.

lessons.topic: Literature reading practice
lessons.description: Apply the course to a guided reading of The Restaurant of Many Orders.

stages.title: 13 · Further coverage gaps
stages.note: Keep these later topics on your roadmap. No matching dedicated public Misa lesson was found; absence from this search is not proof that she never covered them.

lessons.topic: ことはない・ことがある: frequency and necessity
lessons.description: Distinguish occasional occurrences and lack of necessity from past experience.

lessons.topic: に対して・について・によって
lessons.description: Mark a target, topic, or varying basis in longer statements.

lessons.topic: として・にとって
lessons.description: Express a role or the viewpoint from which something matters.

lessons.topic: ばかりでなく・だけでなく・のみならず
lessons.description: Extend a statement with “not only… but also…”.

lessons.topic: くせに・ものの・にもかかわらず
lessons.description: Express different kinds of unexpected contrast.

lessons.topic: 限り・さえ…ば・ない限り
lessons.description: Specify limits and minimum or necessary conditions.

lessons.topic: Advanced formal patterns: に至る・を余儀なくされる
lessons.description: Recognize formal written grammar; no dedicated matching public lesson found.
